chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from 'Ammar al-Sabati said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Every Muslim, son of a Muslim, who apostatizes from Islam and denies the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and disbelieves in him, then his blood is permissible for whoever hears that from him, and his wife is separated from him on the day he apostatizes and one should not approach her, and his wealth is distributed among his heirs, and his wife observes the waiting period of the one whose husband has died, and it is upon the Imam to kill him if he is brought to him, and he does not seek his repentance.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific legal consequences for an apostate regarding marriage, wealth, and execution in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific legal status of the *murtadd* (apostate) by detailing the immediate annulment of marriage (*bina'*) and the distribution of wealth upon apostasy. Notably, it highlights the Shia view that the Imam executes the apostate without prior seeking of repentance (*istitab*), distinguishing this ruling from other schools of thought. The narration underscores the severity of renouncing Islam and the Prophet, rendering the apostate's blood permissible for any Muslim to shed upon hearing the declaration.
